context: A survey of a Grade 10 class records six different things about every learner, so six data sets are collected from the same class. Which six, and which kind of data set is asked about, change between instances.

params.name: names
params.let: ['the number of brothers and sisters', 'the time taken to walk to school, in minutes', 'favourite subject', 'the number of SMS messages sent yesterday', 'the height, in metres', 'a written comment on the lesson', 'the number of books in the school bag', 'the mass of the school bag, in kilograms', 'eye colour', 'the number of times late for school this term', 'the distance from home to school, in kilometres', 'the name of the primary school attended', 'the number of goals scored in the school football season', 'the length of a long jump, in metres', 'the language spoken at home', 'the number of questions answered correctly in a test', 'the volume of water drunk in a day, in litres', 'a short description of a weekend outing']

params.name: rs
params.let: ['counts, written as integers', 'measurements, written as real numbers', 'words or descriptions, not numbers']

params.why: keep the answer between 1 and 4 so it is never 0 or almost everything

stem: A survey of a Grade 10 class records six things about every learner: (a) {=names[order[0]]}; (b) {=names[order[1]]}; (c) {=names[order[2]]}; (d) {=names[order[3]]}; (e) {=names[order[4]]}; (f) {=names[order[5]]}. Each of these six lists of values is a data set. How many of the six data sets are {=asks[a]}? Give your answer as a whole number.
solution: Numbers make a data set quantitative; words or descriptions make it qualitative. A quantitative data set is discrete if it is a count written as integers and continuous if it is a measurement written as real numbers.
Count the data sets that are {=asks[a]}. There are {=total}, so the answer is {=total}.
notes: Advanced tier: several steps. The student classifies six data sets one by one (the book's single-set decision, repeated) and then counts those that match a stated category. The 18-item pool is balanced and interleaved (index mod 3 gives the kind: 0 count, 1 measurement, 2 qualitative) and the six picks are shuffled, so no ordering hint. Every item is an unambiguous count, measurement or non-numeric description: no money, ages, shoe sizes or codes. The asked category varies (discrete, continuous, quantitative of either kind, qualitative) through a weight table, so the same skeleton gives different answers. Numeric, so no distractors and no misconception ids; require keeps the answer between 1 and 4 (about 88% of draws pass).
